surprises.description: Q4 net sales were $333.3 million, above the preview’s $327.1–327.7 million consensus range and the company’s $322–332 million guidance. The 9.7% decline was also less severe than the preview’s implied 11.4% decline.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 fiscal 2026 net sales declined 9.7% to $333.3 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Net sales | Q4 FY26 Consensus | $327.1–327.7M”; company guidance was “$322–332M”; implied YoY was “−11.4%.”

surprises.description: Q4 adjusted EBITDA was $57.5 million, above the preview’s approximately $53 million estimate and slightly above the $52–57 million guidance range. Its 13.2% decline was also less severe than the preview’s implied roughly 20% decline.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA | ~$53M”; company guidance was “$52–57M,” with Q4 FY25 actual “~$66.7M” and implied YoY “−20%.”

surprises.description: FY2027 sales guidance calls for a 13%–17% decline, much weaker than the preview’s working expectation of sales down 2%–5%. This points to a substantially steeper sales contraction than the preview’s base case.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company guided fiscal 2027 net sales to decline 13% to 17%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base case expected “sales −2% to −5%”; it described the Street’s working range as FY27 EBITDA of $200–215 million, with a cautious but credible plan.

surprises.description: FY2027 adjusted EBITDA guidance implies roughly $189–205 million when applied to the preview’s FY2026 guidance range, below the preview’s $200–215 million Street working range for much of the range. Even the top end is only around the bottom of that expectation.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company guided … adjusted EBITDA to decline 9% to 14%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “I’d put the Street’s working range at $200–215M.” The preview gave FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of “$220–225M.”

surprises.description: Management expects Q1 FY2027 to be exceptionally weak, with sales down 19%–22% and adjusted EBITDA down 28%–33%. The preview discussed September pricing and the full-year outlook but did not anticipate a specific quarter with declines this steep.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management expects Q1 fiscal 2027 to be the weakest quarter, with net sales declining 19% to 22% and adjusted EBITDA declining 28% to 33%.”

surprises.description: The September price increase is approaching double digits rather than the preview’s expected high-single-digit increase, and management expects elasticities above the recent approximately 1.2x level, weighted toward the first half. That suggests a heavier near-term volume penalty than the preview’s already-cautious “one or higher” elasticity assumption.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company implemented a price increase approaching double digits across much of its portfolio starting September, expecting elasticities above 1 (higher than the recent ~1.2x) weighted toward the first half.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview discussed the “September high-single-digit price increase” and said “Scalzo flagged elasticity of ‘one or higher.’”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s concerns about persistent protein, packaging, and freight inflation, management expects FY2027 GAAP gross margin to improve 250–300 basis points toward the historic 40% level. The preview had no such full-year margin recovery outlook.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fiscal 2027 GAAP gross margin is expected to improve 250 to 300 basis points toward the historic ~40% level, driven by pricing, productivity, and lower one-time costs.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said “whey spikes” significantly offset cocoa deflation and that “protein, packaging, and freight inflation persist.”

surprises.description: Quest retail takeaway fell 2.1%, missing the preview’s threshold of at least 3% growth for the brand to carry the company. Salty snacks grew about 13%, but bars—which the preview identified as the priority—declined about 6%.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Quest Q4 retail takeaway declined only 2.1% with household penetration up ~50 bps to 20.2%, while salty snacks grew ~13% and bars declined ~6%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Quest needs to be ≥+3% for the ‘Quest carries the company’ thesis to work”; the preview also called bars “the bulk of the brand” and said they were “the highest priority.”

surprises.description: Atkins household penetration fell about 210 basis points to 8.3%, an additional sign of deterioration even as retail takeaway narrowed slightly from Q3. The preview focused on whether the decline rate was stabilizing but did not flag this penetration drop.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Atkins Q4 retail takeaway fell 22.6% with household penetration down ~210 bps to 8.3%, though buy rate remained stable.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked “Atkins decline rate — has the bleeding stopped?” and said to watch for the decline to narrow to the “high-teens/low-20s.”

surprises.description: The company ended the year with lower net leverage and more cash than the preview indicated, despite completing about $213 million of repurchases. Net debt was approximately 0.9x EBITDA rather than the preview’s 1.2x, and cash was $138.4 million rather than $123.9 million.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended fiscal 2026 with $138.4 million cash, net debt of ~0.9x EBITDA … repurchased 11.7 million shares for ~$213 million.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview listed “net debt/EBITDA 1.2x, cash $123.9M” and “$213M repurchased YTD.”
